subject: biology
title: Producer
summary: A producer is a living thing that makes its own food - most often by using sunlight through photosynthesis. Explore how plants and other producers capture energy and feed the whole ecosystem.

crossReferences.label: Consumer (Ecology)
crossReferences.note: Consumers cannot make their own food - they eat producers or other consumers.

crossReferences.label: Decomposer (Ecology)
crossReferences.note: When a producer dies, decomposers break it down and recycle its nutrients.

compareCandidate.label: Producer vs. consumer
compareCandidate.description: A producer makes its own food from sunlight and simple ingredients. A consumer cannot - it must eat other living things to get energy.

plainLanguageExplanation: A producer makes its own food. The most common producers are green plants, which use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make their own food (sugar) through photosynthesis. Algae, phytoplankton, and some bacteria are also producers. Because producers create food from sunlight and simple ingredients, they are the first link in every food chain - everything else ultimately depends on them for energy. Without producers, there would be no food for anything else.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: Makes its own food, usually with sunlight

keyFacts.label: How
keyFacts.value: Photosynthesis: sunlight + water + carbon dioxide -> food

keyFacts.label: Place in chain
keyFacts.value: The first link in every food chain

keyFacts.label: Why they matter
keyFacts.value: They turn sunlight into energy everything else can use

whyItMatters: Producers are the foundation of all life - they capture sunlight and turn it into food. Understanding producers explains why food chains start with plants and why every animal depends on them.
didYouKnow: The grass you see everywhere is a producer - and about 8,000 blades of grass can be packed into one square meter of lawn.
